description: Deployable headless backend (Hono) that orchestrates a fleet of agents from markdown packs. API-only — no UI. Routes /chat to single agents or multi-agent team rosters. Single egress through router.tangle.tools. Sister to agent-platform-ts (which has the dashboard). For Slack bots, CLIs, or custom frontends that need agent orchestration as a service.

buildHints.whenToUse: Headless backend that fronts a fleet of markdown-pack agents. Ship this when the consumer (Slack bot, CLI, custom frontend) does NOT want a dashboard — they just want HTTP/JSON. For the dashboarded sister, use `agent-platform-ts`. For a single agent with a chat UI, use `agent-with-ui-ts`.
firstSteps: Set TANGLE_ROUTER_KEY (router.tangle.tools key) and AGENT_PACK_DIR (filesystem dir holding agent packs).
Drop an agent pack into AGENT_PACK_DIR: either `<id>/system-prompt.md` (single agent) or `<id>/agent-roster.json` (team).
Run `pnpm dev`; curl POST /chat with `{ "agent": "<id>", "messages": [...] }` and stream the response.
Lock down before prod: see docs/SECURITY.md (API-key header is a starter, not a finish line).
gotchas: chat-bridge.ts is the only file allowed to call router.tangle.tools. If you reach for fetch() elsewhere, the single-egress invariant is dead.
Rate limit is in-memory by default — multi-instance deploys MUST swap in Redis or the bucket is per-instance, not per-tenant.
HMAC webhooks have no nonce table; the 5-minute replay window is the only defense against replay. Document this for downstream operators.
agent-roster.json without `defaultRespondent` falls back to LLM-routing — every /chat to that team pays a cheap routing call before the real call.
architectureNotes: Hono runs on Bun, Node, AND Cloudflare Workers — pick the adapter at deploy time. Wrangler config ships for the Workers path; package.json scripts cover Node + Bun.
Agent loader returns a discriminated union: `{ kind: 'single', ... } | { kind: 'team', roles: [...] }`. Downstream router.ts dispatches on `kind`.
Audit log writes to filesystem by default (local dev). For prod, swap audit.ts's sink for S3/Postgres — the function signature is the seam.
